page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6t.13xlarge is an instance within the Enhanced family running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 52 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.69 GB of RAM per vCPU, without bundled hardware GPUs.

Storage and networking profiles require consideration of cloud-attached infrastructure. The instance features no local disk storage, meaning persistent storage requirements must be fulfilled via network-attached storage volumes. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned directly with the instance.

Resource allocation is balanced between compute and memory, avoiding the performance variability of shared-core hosts due to its dedicated CPU threads. The ecs.g6t.13xlarge is suited for concurrent enterprise applications, large web serving clusters, intermediate database operations relying on remote block storage, and multi-threaded data processing pipelines.
description: The Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6t.13xlarge is an instance within the Enhanced family powered by the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running at 2.5 GHz. It provides 52 dedicated vCPUs paired with 192.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a ratio of approximately 3.69 GB of memory per core. The server does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating external network-attached storage for operating system and application data, and it includes no discrete hardware GPUs. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps. The architecture balances heavy thread counts with dedicated resource allocations, eliminating contention typical of shared configurations. Given its hardware density, balanced memory footprint, and network capacity, the ecs.g6t.13xlarge suits multi-threaded enterprise services, backend application runtimes, large-scale web serving tiers, and containerized microservice deployments requiring sustained computing power.
